disposition: The article and noun also look singular in the new crop. Prefer soit, with sont retained.
The tall first stroke can be l or b; base is an additional candidate.
The enlarged D has two uprights. Keep the double-stem alphabet in the file.
The same double upright recurs. The narrow tilde is distinct.
A short cross-stroke beneath hatching could be a minus. Retain (-1) first and the blind (1) second.
Both slots have a numeral-like stroke; the second can also be t. Add the alternative at the final slot.
The apparent comma is part of the first closing parenthesis. Retain three adjacent references.
There is a detached dot; keep la first and add ici.
The blind probe identifies the double-stem capital only. The lower loop or loops following it belong to a subscript. Keep the alternatives 3 and 8 on that subscript.
A long descender below the cancellation favours que or par over sur.
The tall looped L is consistent over the three occurrences. Retain the script alphabet.
The return below the tall L agrees with the other script L's. The arrow faces left.
The u and its barred map are continuous across a typesetting alignment. The letters and arrow agree in both readings.
Remove the spurious cancelled duplicate. The long line returns to the g in Legendre one line above.
No independent underline is visible on the set in the box; the parenthesis starts before the equals sign.
Retain de là and admit et là. No u is isolated at the right.
The cancelled loop has a tail; add δ without deciding for it.
The rotated crop separates e from the tall b in base. Prefer e, retain b.
The dot above ξ is distinct and the subscript I has no additional line.
The low hook is the foot of I without an underline.
The dark patch cancels only the upper dual sign, leaving a single live F.
The raised-contrast crop 097_nb_signs.jpg shows two separate horizontal rules, beneath ω and beneath its index I. Keep both rules. The blind probe omitted them.
Two different forms of raised mark, one cross and one star.
The strokes join to d'une and there is no independent cancellation.
Reverse the candidate order for the looped δ.
The right member has the same letter, δ, written with a rounder loop.
The surviving long stem permits κ; keep the blind ω as an alternative.
The end of the word is crossed; add de as an alternative.
The crossed loop also permits à.
The blind probe omitted the small def placed over the equality.
The insert has one enclosing pair; no second parenthesis is visible next to 72.
The final stem may be the f of an unfinished word. Keep satisf first and add satisfont.
Prefer à deux élé under the crossing; retain des él. as an alternative.
A distinct t and terminal stroke favour ments, the remnant of the overwritten adjective phrase.
The first N of Nous is written over a short older capital; allons is the separate word after it.
The cropped deletion continues after un, with a second tall stroke compatible with loi.
A second bend permits ξ or the alternate epsilon; keep all three.
The final n and an older return in its subscript are distinguishable.
The initial before on was retraced. Keep both readings.
The right curl could be a 2 or a vertical isomorphism sign. Keep both.
